source_text: 24 QUI IMENTET. ? NON CREDENT Quamdiu, stulte homo, Christum cognoscere non uis? Uitas agrum pinguem et stereli semina iactas. In silua manere quaeris, ubi latro moratur. Ingredere iam nunc totiens inuitatus in aula: Matura iam messis, tempus totidemque paratum, Ecce modo mete, quodsi non te paenitet inde. Nunc, si non habes, collige; uindemia uenit; Tempus adest uitae credenti tempore mortis. Est Dei lex prima fundamentum posterae legis, Teque designabat, crederes in lege secunda; Nec minus et ipsos et ex ipsa sibi prudentes Obstupe iam factus ora tu credere Christo, Nam testamentum uetus de isto proclamat. Credere nun<c> opus est, tantum in isto defunctum Resurgere posse <et> uiuere tempore toto. Ergo si quis ea discredis esse futura Dummodo uincetur reus in morte secunda, Euentura canam paucis in isto libello Nam cognosci potest, ubi sit spes uitae ponenda. Tamen uos adhortor quantocius credere Christo.
pass_a_gloss: How long, stulte, refuse Christum cognoscere? Avoid rich field; stay in robber’s wood. Enter aula; harvest ripe; tempus vitae credenti tempore mortis. First law founds later; OT proclaims him — ora tu credere Christo. Need to believe dead can rise in him; else reus in morte secunda. Ubi sit spes vitae; quantocius credere Christo.
pass_b_english: How long, foolish man, will you refuse to know Christ? You avoid the rich field and cast seed on the barren. You want to stay in the wood where the robber lurks. Enter already now into the hall, so often invited: the harvest is already ripe, the time equally prepared — see, reap now, if you do not then regret it. Now, if you have nothing, gather; the vintage comes; the time of life is at hand for the believer in the time of death.

God’s first law is the foundation of the later law, and it marked you out that you should believe in the second law; and no less did it stun those from that law who were wise for themselves. Now become stunned and speak — believe in Christ — for the old testament proclaims concerning him. Now there is need to believe — only that the dead can rise in him and live for the whole time. Therefore if anyone refuses to believe these things will be, while he is beaten as guilty in the second death, I will sing in a few words in this little book what will come — for it can be known where the hope of life must be set. Still I urge you as soon as possible to believe in Christ.

lemmas.sense: time of life for the believer

choices.choose: life for the believer at death’s time
choices.why: Tempus adest uitae credenti tempore mortis.
ubi sit spes uitae ponenda; resurgere posse.
